rationale:
The supplied proof has three separate obligations of different kinds. Each is a general, reusable fact; the assembly from them is short.

1. level_split (parent steps 2–3). A test form whose support misses {f = t} splits into a piece supported in {f < t} and a piece supported in {t < f}. This is pure smooth topology, with no currents or measures. The split is done with a smooth Urysohn function. The child proof takes the separating closed sets as K ∩ {f ≤ t} and K ∩ {t ≤ f}, where K = tsupport η. This removes the parent's δ-margin, compactness step and K = ∅ case; the independent reviewer judged this a legitimate specialization.

2. boundary_inside (parent steps 1 and 5). For any set S, ∂(T⌞S)(θ) = (∂T)⌞S(θ) whenever tsupport θ ⊆ S.

3. vanish_outside (parent steps 1 and 4). For any set S, ∂(T⌞S)(θ) = 0 and (∂T)⌞S(θ) = 0 whenever tsupport θ misses S.

The parent (step 6) then follows by linearity. With S := {f < t}, child 2 is applied to η₁ and child 3 to η₂, using tsupport η₂ ⊆ {t < f}.

Reuse: the DAG nodes dor_lmb_slicing_lipschitz and dimred_mbl_slice_mass_bounds need the same slice-support property, so level_split (and children 2 and 3) are directly relevant to them.

subproblems.title: Level-set splitting of a test form whose support misses {f = t}
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be continuous, let t ∈ ℝ, and let η ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (a C^∞ n-form on ℝ^P with compact support whose topological support lies in U) be such that tsupport η is disjoint from {x : f(x) = t}. Then there are η₁, η₂ ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with η = η₁ + η₂, tsupport η₁ ⊆ {x : f(x) < t} and tsupport η₂ ⊆ {x : t < f(x)}.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (t : ℝ) (η : TestFormOn U n), Continuous f → Disjoint (tsupport (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) {x | f x = t} → ∃ η₁ η₂ : TestFormOn U n, η = η₁ + η₂ ∧ tsupport (η₁ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ {x | f x < t} ∧ tsupport (η₂ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ {x | t < f x}
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–3 of the parent proof of cmcs_slice_support (splitting η with a smooth Urysohn function), specialized as follows: the two separating closed sets are taken inside K := tsupport η̂, so the parent's δ-margin is not needed. For a form θ write θ̂ for its underlying map ℝ^P → Λ^n(ℝ^P). Membership θ ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (TestFormOn U n) means three things: θ̂ is C^∞ (IsSmoothForm, i.e. ContDiff ℝ ∞), θ̂ has compact support (HasCompactSupport), and tsupport θ̂ ⊆ U. Addition in 𝒟^n(U) is pointwise addition of the underlying forms.
1. (The two halves of the support.) Let K := tsupport η̂; it is closed (isClosed_tsupport). Put K₋ := K ∩ {x : f(x) ≤ t} and K₊ := K ∩ {x : t ≤ f(x)}.
   (a) Both sets are closed: f is continuous, so {f ≤ t} and {t ≤ f} are closed (isClosed_le).
   (b) They are disjoint: a common point x would lie in K and satisfy f(x) ≤ t ≤ f(x), i.e. x ∈ K ∩ {f = t}, contradicting the hypothesis.
   (c) Every x ∈ K₋ satisfies f(x) < t: we have f(x) ≤ t, and f(x) ≠ t because x ∈ K is not in {f = t}.
   (d) In the same way, every x ∈ K₊ satisfies t < f(x).
2. (Smooth Urysohn function.) The space ℝ^P is finite-dimensional. Apply the smooth Urysohn lemma, Mathlib exists_contDiff_zero_iff_one_iff_of_isClosed, with smoothness order ⊤ : ℕ∞, taking as the lemma's first closed set s := K₊ and as its second closed set K₋. Both are closed by step 1(a) and disjoint by step 1(b). (The lemma's own name for its second set is t; it is unrelated to the level t.) It gives a C^∞ function χ : ℝ^P → ℝ with χ(x) = 0 for every x ∈ K₊ and χ(x) = 1 for every x ∈ K₋. Only these two implications are used.
3. (The pieces are test forms.) Define η̂₁(x) := χ(x)·η̂(x) and η̂₂(x) := (1 − χ(x))·η̂(x).
   (a) Both maps are C^∞: χ and 1 − χ are smooth scalar functions and η̂ is a smooth form (ContDiff.smul).
   (b) If η̂(x) = 0 then c·η̂(x) = 0 for every scalar c, so support η̂ᵢ ⊆ support η̂. Hence both maps have compact support (HasCompactSupport.smul_left), and tsupport η̂ᵢ ⊆ tsupport η̂ ⊆ U (tsupport_smul_subset_right).
   (c) So they define η₁, η₂ ∈ 𝒟^n(U).
   (d) For every x, η̂₁(x) + η̂₂(x) = (χ(x) + (1 − χ(x)))·η̂(x) = η̂(x). Hence η = η₁ + η₂, as an equality of elements of the subtype (Subtype.ext, funext, add_smul).
4. (Support of the lower piece.) Let x satisfy η̂₁(x) ≠ 0.
   (a) Then η̂(x) ≠ 0, so x ∈ support η̂ ⊆ K, and χ(x) ≠ 0.
   (b) If t ≤ f(x), then x ∈ K₊, so χ(x) = 0 by step 2, which is impossible. Hence f(x) < t, in particular f(x) ≤ t, so x ∈ K₋.
   (c) Thus support η̂₁ ⊆ K₋. Since K₋ is closed, tsupport η̂₁ = closure(support η̂₁) ⊆ K₋ (closure_minimal).
   (d) By step 1(c), K₋ ⊆ {x : f(x) < t}, so tsupport η̂₁ ⊆ {x : f(x) < t}.
5. (Support of the upper piece.) Let x satisfy η̂₂(x) ≠ 0.
   (a) Then η̂(x) ≠ 0, so x ∈ K, and 1 − χ(x) ≠ 0, i.e. χ(x) ≠ 1.
   (b) If f(x) ≤ t, then x ∈ K₋, so χ(x) = 1 by step 2, which is impossible. Hence t < f(x), so x ∈ K₊.
   (c) Thus support η̂₂ ⊆ K₊. Since K₊ is closed, tsupport η̂₂ ⊆ K₊.
   (d) By step 1(d), K₊ ⊆ {x : t < f(x)}, so tsupport η̂₂ ⊆ {x : t < f(x)}.
6. (Conclusion.) η₁ and η₂ lie in 𝒟^n(U) (step 3) and satisfy η = η₁ + η₂, tsupport η̂₁ ⊆ {x : f(x) < t} (step 4) and tsupport η̂₂ ⊆ {x : t < f(x)} (step 5). ∎
proof_key_steps: K := tsupport η is closed. The sets K₋ := K ∩ {f ≤ t} and K₊ := K ∩ {t ≤ f} are closed and disjoint, because K misses {f = t}. Moreover K₋ ⊆ {f < t} and K₊ ⊆ {t < f}.
The smooth Urysohn lemma (exists_contDiff_zero_iff_one_iff_of_isClosed) gives a C^∞ function χ with χ = 0 on K₊ and χ = 1 on K₋.
η₁ := χ·η and η₂ := (1 − χ)·η are smooth and compactly supported, with tsupport ⊆ tsupport η ⊆ U. So both are test forms in U, and η = η₁ + η₂.
support(χ·η) ⊆ K₋ and support((1 − χ)·η) ⊆ K₊. Both sets are closed, so tsupport η₁ ⊆ K₋ ⊆ {f < t} and tsupport η₂ ⊆ K₊ ⊆ {t < f}.

subproblems.title: Inside S the boundary of the restriction T⌞S agrees with (∂T)⌞S
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ and let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set. Let T ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U), let μ, μ' be measures on ℝ^P, and let ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_{k+1}(ℝ^P) and ξ' : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) be arbitrary maps such that T(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(U) and ∂T(θ) = ∫ ξ'(x)(θ(x)) dμ'(x) for every θ ∈ 𝒟^k(U) (Bochner integrals). Let S ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, and let A ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U), B ∈ 𝒟_k(U) satisfy A(ω) = ∫_S ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(U) and B(θ) = ∫_S ξ'(x)(θ(x)) dμ'(x) for every θ ∈ 𝒟^k(U). Then ∂A(θ) = B(θ) for every θ ∈ 𝒟^k(U) with tsupport θ ⊆ S.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U (k + 1)) (μ μ' : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P (k + 1)) (ξ' : Euclid P → MultiVector P k) (S : Set (Euclid P)) (A : GeometricCurrentOn U (k + 1)) (B : GeometricCurrentOn U k), (∀ ω : TestFormOn U (k + 1), T ω = ∫ x, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (k + 1)) x) ∂μ) → (∀ θ : TestFormOn U k, T.boundary θ = ∫ x, ξ' x ((θ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ') → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U (k + 1), A ω = ∫ x in S, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (k + 1)) x) ∂μ) → (∀ θ : TestFormOn U k, B θ = ∫ x in S, ξ' x ((θ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ') → ∀ θ : TestFormOn U k, tsupport (θ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) ⊆ S → A.boundary θ = B θ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 5 of the parent proof of cmcs_slice_support, with the set {f < t} replaced by an arbitrary set S and η₋ replaced by an arbitrary θ ∈ 𝒟^k(U) with tsupport θ̂ ⊆ S. For a form θ write θ̂ for its underlying map ℝ^P → Λ^k(ℝ^P).
0. (Boundary.) Write dθ := exteriorDerivativeTestOn U k θ ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(U); its underlying form is exteriorDerivative θ̂. By GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply (a definitional equality), ∂A(θ) = A(dθ) and ∂T(θ) = T(dθ).
1. (Vanishing off S.) Let x ∉ S.
   (a) Since tsupport θ̂ ⊆ S, x ∉ tsupport θ̂, so θ̂(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport).
   (b) Since tsupport(exteriorDerivative θ̂) ⊆ tsupport θ̂ (SimonGMT tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset), also x ∉ tsupport(exteriorDerivative θ̂), so (exteriorDerivative θ̂)(x) = 0.
   (c) ξ(x) and ξ'(x) are linear maps. Hence ξ(x)((exteriorDerivative θ̂)(x)) = ξ(x)(0) = 0 and ξ'(x)(θ̂(x)) = ξ'(x)(0) = 0.
2. (Integrals over S equal integrals over ℝ^P.) Let ν be any measure and G : ℝ^P → ℝ any function with G(x) = 0 for every x ∉ S. Then ∫_S G dν = ∫ G dν (Mathlib setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero; no integrability or measurability hypothesis is needed). By step 1 this applies to G(x) := ξ(x)((exteriorDerivative θ̂)(x)) with ν := μ, and to G(x) := ξ'(x)(θ̂(x)) with ν := μ'.
3. (Chain of equalities.) Each equality below is justified by, in order: step 0; the representation of A applied to ω := dθ; step 2; the representation of T applied to ω := dθ; step 0; the representation of ∂T applied to θ; step 2; the representation of B applied to θ.
∂A(θ) = A(dθ) = ∫_S ξ(x)((exteriorDerivative θ̂)(x)) dμ(x) = ∫ ξ(x)((exteriorDerivative θ̂)(x)) dμ(x) = T(dθ) = ∂T(θ) = ∫ ξ'(x)(θ̂(x)) dμ'(x) = ∫_S ξ'(x)(θ̂(x)) dμ'(x) = B(θ). ∎
proof_key_steps: ∂A(θ) = A(dθ) and ∂T(θ) = T(dθ), where dθ is the test form with underlying map exteriorDerivative θ̂ (boundary_apply).
Off S both θ̂ and exteriorDerivative θ̂ vanish, because tsupport θ̂ ⊆ S and tsupport(exteriorDerivative θ̂) ⊆ tsupport θ̂. Since ξ(x) and ξ'(x) are linear, both integrands vanish off S.
So both integrals over S equal the integrals over ℝ^P (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero).
∂A(θ) = ∫_S ξ(dθ̂) dμ = ∫ ξ(dθ̂) dμ = T(dθ) = ∂T(θ) = ∫ ξ'(θ̂) dμ' = ∫_S ξ'(θ̂) dμ' = B(θ).

subproblems.title: Off S both ∂(T⌞S) and (∂T)⌞S vanish
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ and let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set. Let μ, μ' be measures on ℝ^P, let ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_{k+1}(ℝ^P) and ξ' : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) be arbitrary maps, and let S ⊆ ℝ^P be any set. Let A ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U) and B ∈ 𝒟_k(U) satisfy A(ω) = ∫_S ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(U) and B(θ) = ∫_S ξ'(x)(θ(x)) dμ'(x) for every θ ∈ 𝒟^k(U) (Bochner integrals). Then ∂A(θ) = 0 and B(θ) = 0 for every θ ∈ 𝒟^k(U) whose topological support tsupport θ is disjoint from S.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (μ μ' : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P (k + 1)) (ξ' : Euclid P → MultiVector P k) (S : Set (Euclid P)) (A : GeometricCurrentOn U (k + 1)) (B : GeometricCurrentOn U k), (∀ ω : TestFormOn U (k + 1), A ω = ∫ x in S, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (k + 1)) x) ∂μ) → (∀ θ : TestFormOn U k, B θ = ∫ x in S, ξ' x ((θ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ') → ∀ θ : TestFormOn U k, Disjoint (tsupport (θ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k)) S → A.boundary θ = 0 ∧ B θ = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 4 of the parent proof of cmcs_slice_support, with the set {f < t} replaced by an arbitrary set S and η₊ replaced by an arbitrary θ ∈ 𝒟^k(U) whose support misses S. For a form θ write θ̂ for its underlying map ℝ^P → Λ^k(ℝ^P). Write dθ := exteriorDerivativeTestOn U k θ ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(U); its underlying form is exteriorDerivative θ̂, and ∂A(θ) = A(dθ) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply, a definitional equality).
1. (Vanishing on S.) Let x ∈ S.
   (a) Since tsupport θ̂ ∩ S = ∅, x ∉ tsupport θ̂, hence θ̂(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport).
   (b) Since tsupport(exteriorDerivative θ̂) ⊆ tsupport θ̂ (SimonGMT tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset), x ∉ tsupport(exteriorDerivative θ̂), hence (exteriorDerivative θ̂)(x) = 0.
   (c) ξ(x) and ξ'(x) are linear. Hence ξ(x)((exteriorDerivative θ̂)(x)) = 0 and ξ'(x)(θ̂(x)) = 0 for all x ∈ S.
2. (Boundary term.) The representation of A applied to ω := dθ gives
∂A(θ) = A(dθ) = ∫_S ξ(x)((exteriorDerivative θ̂)(x)) dμ(x).
The integrand vanishes at every point of S by step 1, so this integral is 0 by Mathlib setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero (no integrability is needed).
3. (Restricted boundary term.) By the representation of B, B(θ) = ∫_S ξ'(x)(θ̂(x)) dμ'(x). This is 0 by step 1 and setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero.
4. (Conclusion.) ∂A(θ) = 0 and B(θ) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: On S, θ̂ = 0 and exteriorDerivative θ̂ = 0, because S misses tsupport θ̂ ⊇ tsupport(exteriorDerivative θ̂).
∂A(θ) = A(dθ) = ∫_S ξ(dθ̂) dμ = 0, since the integrand vanishes on S (setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero).
B(θ) = ∫_S ξ'(θ̂) dμ' = 0, for the same reason.
